Thanks again for taking the time today  great conversation. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can continue qualification on access controls and support access for FinTrust's pilot: 

1) PII & data residency: You confirmed the pilot will process customer PII (names, emails, account IDs) and you'd like to keep data in US regions only.
2) Logging & retention: You require audit logs for all user activity and 13 months of retention for customer visibility.
3) Access model: You asked about RBAC for customer seats, least-privilege defaults, support access with break-glass, and the ability to restrict Redwood support to metadata-only unless explicitly authorized.

Next steps I propose:
- Dev / Engineering will provide a short access-matrix & support-access runbook by EOD Wednesday.
- I'll share our SOC 2 summary and the relevant RBAC docs (see attachments).
- Schedule: Can we target a 30min technical follow-up on Thursday (your timezone) to walk the runbook?

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary), access-matrix.xlsx (RBAC + support access mapping).

Open items we plan to cover in follow-up: default roles, break-glass escalation flow, audit log delivery (S3/BigQuery or API), and encryption/KMS controls for stored data.

Hi Sanjay  jumping in with technical details so the follow-up call can focus on any gaps: 

Summary answers: 
- Break-glass & auditing: Support break-glass is gated by an internal runbook + automated approval workflow. When break-glass is used we: (1) require an approved ticket (Doc) that includes justification, (2) capture the operator identity and session start/end times, (3) record all accessed object identifiers and commands executed, and (4) emit an immutable audit record to your configured audit sink (S3 or our BigQuery export). Audit records are signed and retained per configured retention.

- RBAC scoping: Our RBAC model supports multi-tenant scoping  roles can be defined at organization, account (customer), and project level. Default roles are read-only analyst, app-integration, and admin. Custom roles allow granular permissions (view logs, request support access, create API keys).

- Least privilege & support access: By default, Redwood support accounts have metadata-only visibility. For elevated actions we require a documented break-glass that is time-limited and audited. We also support time-bound short-lived access tokens (OIDC-based) and can restrict sessions to IP ranges if you require.

- Log export/retention: We support scheduled exports to S3 (daily/weekly/monthly) and on-demand snapshots. Retention policies are configurable; default retention for audit events can be set to 13 months to match your requirement.

I've attached a short access-matrix (access-matrix.xlsx) and a 1-page break-glass runbook excerpt. Bringing Priyom on the call for policy/contract alignment.

Best,
